objective: At the owner's request ('Yes, please continue.', approving CHAIN-TRANSFER-20261106-001's recommendation): read the atoms, and so the genus, through plane glue. Bring plane pieces into the analysis of creation, explain the glue line that joins an atom's twin class and the atoms that split into twin pairs, and look for one rule that reads the atoms of every three-fold space; prove what can be proved and test the rest on the census and on larger spaces. No time constraints.
status: Complete 2026-11-06: partially successful. Creation at a Fano atom is decided by its cut: whether a removal beyond a cut creates at a line of the atom depends only on the patterns the removal's side allows on the cut's three ports (proved exhaustively; 47,550 census pairs agree). Through atoms the cut is always free, so the touching rule holds; plane glue can exclude a pattern pair or tie two ports, and the touching rule then fails exactly as the law says. The two-stage twin rule reads every Fano tree with at most four cuts per atom, all 111 census spaces and 57 of 80 random glued spaces; in 15 random spaces lines of atoms meeting one planar brace are indistinguishable to whether creation occurs, so no yes/no rule reads them, though which far side creates separates them. Next: reading with the far sides (2/3)
stop_rule: Stop when a reading rule through plane glue is proved, refuted, or reduced to named unproved statements with their evidence; and when what plane glue does to creation is stated with its exact proof status.
